subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: FinWise performance targets & customer-led load test
messages:
From: Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudOps Team <cloudops@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can schedule a customer-led load test: 

- Targets: p95 latency <= 200ms for generation (non-streaming), p99 <= 400ms.
- Throughput: target sustained 1200 requests/minute during peak 15-min windows, with burst up to 2000 r/min for 2 minutes.
- Concurrency: load will be ~25 concurrent streaming sessions (SSE) for live UI use, plus up to 400 concurrent non-streaming requests.
- Streaming: we need server-sent events with chunked tokens — ensure Redwood streaming endpoints support downstream reconnects and partial tokens.

What we need from you to run the test from our side:
1) A Redwood test account with access to the same model variant you demoed (pin to v2027-04) and a test API key.
2) IP ranges to allowlist on our side (we will provide our CloudOps IP block but need yours).
3) Example k6 or Locust scripts and a sample test-account CSV so our load team can ramp.
4) A 2-hour window next week (we prefer Tue/Wed morning PST).

Attaching our expected workload profile as notes in the body — we can share more specifics once we have the test key.

Thanks,
Ari
Director, Platform Engineering
FinWise
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Ari — great to sync. Appreciate the detailed targets. Quick responses and proposed next steps: 

- Test account & key: we can provision a scoped test API key tied to a sandbox project and pin the model to v2027-04. It will have rate limits removed for the test window.
- IP allowlist: attaching our public IP ranges as a file (redwood-ip-allowlist.txt). Please confirm the format your firewall needs.
- Scripts & accounts: attaching a k6 script (k6-fs-load-test.js) and a sample test-accounts CSV (test-accounts-redwood.csv). These are meant to be a starting point — Rishi will suggest tweaks for streaming.
- Windows: Tue 2027-06-08 08:00–10:00 PST or Wed 2027-06-09 08:00–10:00 PST both work for us. Which do you prefer?

Notes on SLOs and config: for streaming SSE sessions we recommend a separate curve in k6 to simulate long-lived connections (ramp to 25 concurrent for 30–45 minutes). For non-streaming generation load, the k6 script includes a 15-min steady-state step at 1200 r/min and two 2-min spike stages to 2000 r/min.

We’ll also provide a short Prometheus + Grafana link to view token-level latency and request traces during the window. Rishi — can you confirm the sampling & tracing endpoints we should expose for them?

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Logan — thanks, that all looks good. A couple clarifications from CloudOps: 

- Streaming: we need the ability to resume streams if a TCP connection drops and for Redwood to support sending back a last-token id or offset so the client can request missing tokens. Does Redwood support partial token replay or a reconnect token?
- Observability: can you push traces to our OTLP collector (we run a collector in our VPC)? If not, can you provide a webhook for traces?

We’ll take Wed 2027-06-09 08:00–10:00 PST to avoid other deployments on Tue. We’ll confirm a final attendee list by EOD Friday.

—Sam
CloudOps Manager, FinWise
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finwise.com>, Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Sam — we can support reconnect semantics for streaming at the application level. For this test we’ll provide a reconnect token scheme: on initial stream open the server returns a stream_id and last_offset. On reconnect you can pass stream_id + last_offset and we’ll replay missing tokens up to a short buffer (configurable per test). I’ll have Rishi include an example payload in the scripts.

Observability: we can forward OTLP traces to your collector for the test window (we’ll need an endpoint and auth header). If firewalls block outbound we can instead upload a trace bundle to the Drive link in related_links for immediate review.

I’ll also provision a short-lived test project in our Dedicated sandbox so you can hit the exact runtime we use in prod for inference (same kernel selection / quant profiles). That should give you realistic latency.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finwise.com>, Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Following up with the technical details and the scripts attached: 

- k6-fs-load-test.js (attached): has two scenarios — streaming_sse (25 virtual users, long-lived connections, send/receive heartbeat every 30s) and batch_gen (stages to reach 1200 r/min). I added a reconnect example that POSTS the last_offset when reconnecting.
- test-accounts-redwood.csv: includes 50 synthetic test identities (user_id, session_token_stub). We’ll create real test keys for the accounts and pass them to your team 24 hours before the test.
- IP allowlist: redwood-ip-allowlist.txt contains our egress ranges for the sandbox project; confirm these in your firewall.

Suggestion for monitoring: please capture p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and full-response times, and include network RTT. We’ll export traces to your OTLP endpoint; please email me the collector endpoint and an HMAC header to use.

If you want, we can run a short smoke test Tue 2027-06-08 16:00–16:15 PST to validate connectivity and keys. Otherwise we’ll proceed with Wed 08:00 main run.

—Rishi
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Ari Johnson <ari.johnson@finwise.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudOps Team <cloudops@finwise.com>, Samantha Lee <sam.lee@finwise.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance targets & next steps

Thanks, team — Wed 2027-06-09 08:00–10:00 PST confirmed. A few items: 

- Our CloudOps IP ranges: 18.205.0.0/16, 54.213.0.0/16 (we’ll open outbound). Please confirm redwood-ip-allowlist.txt includes 3rd-party egress for the sandbox (we saw a few ranges).
- OTLP endpoint: https://otlp.finwise.internal:4317 (we’ll send a pre-shared HMAC via secure vault).
- We’ll take the smoke test Tue 2027-06-08 16:00–16:15 PST to validate keys and connectivity.
- HubSpot deal: I created a task under FW-2027-0423 to capture the post-test findings and next steps.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the run.

Best,
Ari
Director, Platform Engineering, FinWise
